caption_v6_tex:
\textbf{Calibration after a maximum over layers subtracts a threshold that follows the largest random-pairing
baseline, in all three families (Proposition~\ref{prop:baselines}, Corollary~\ref{cor:aggregation}).}
This full version of Figure~\ref{fig:exp-aggregation} has one column per language-model family.
(a--c) Size trend $\mathrm{Tr}$ of each score before calibration (ring), after subtraction of the permutation mean
(dot) and under $s_{\rm cal}$ (tick), with $95\%$ intervals over vision models (tints). The grey bands in (a) span the
one-sided $5\%$ critical values of the relabelling null over the BLOOMZ sizes.
(d--f) Means over vision models of the observed layer maximum of CKA, of its threshold $c_\alpha$ (squares), of the
largest baseline predicted from single-model features (grey line) and of the threshold of the layer pair attaining the
maximum (dotted line). On BLOOMZ the readings of (d) and (g) are post hoc (tag), whereas in the other two families
the grey line was frozen from features before scoring. Where the squares sit well above the dotted line, the threshold comes from layer
pairs other than the pair attaining the maximum.
(g--i) CKA baseline of each language-model layer under random pairing, predicted from features by
Proposition~\ref{prop:baselines} (one line per size) and measured by permutation (dots), with a square on the largest
baseline of each size and shading over the depths of the observed maximum. The mKNN baseline (blue) is the same at
every layer. Rows marked expl.\ are exploratory.
Appendices~\ref{app:exp-layermax} and~\ref{app:exp-openllama} give the values, the tests and the standard errors.

caption_v8.tex: \caption{\textbf{After a maximum over layers, the calibration threshold follows the largest random-pairing baseline in all three families (Proposition~\ref{prop:baselines}, Corollary~\ref{cor:aggregation}).} This full version of Figure~\ref{fig:exp-aggregation} adds the rows for calibration before the maximum, CKA at the last layer, and debiased CKA. (a--c) The subtraction removes the permutation mean. (d--f) Squares give the threshold $c_\alpha$, dashed lines the largest baseline predicted from features, and dotted lines the threshold of the selected layer pair. (g--i) CKA baseline of each language-model layer, predicted (lines) and measured (dots). Appendices~\ref{app:exp-layermax} and~\ref{app:exp-openllama} give the values.}
